highlight.text: Giotto's Crucifix at Santa Maria Novella is a cross painted in tempera and gold on wood panel (578 x 406 cm) by Giotto di Bondone around 1290–1295.

work.text: It is one of the earliest known works by the artist, then in his early twenties.

source.title: Giotto's Crucifix at Santa Maria Novella

moment.text: In contrast to the iconography now "canonized" by Giunta Pisano of the Christus patiens sinuously arched to the left (for the observer), Giotto paints the corpse vertically, legs bent, allowing the full weight to be released.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors

moment.text: he banished completely that rude Greek manner and revived the modern and good art of painting

source.author: Giorgio Vasari
source.title: Life of Giotto, in Lives of the Most Eminent Painters, Sculptors and Architects (trans. Gaston du C. de Vere)

moment.lead: Vasari on the effect of Giotto's training:

matters.text: Only the Aureola recalls his divine nature, but Giotto shows a humble man who truly suffers, with whom the observer can compare his pain.
